title: Lesson 13. JavaScript — variables, types, operators
description: let, const, data types, typeof, arithmetic, === and template strings

learn.intro: Hi! Lesson 13 — **JavaScript**. HTML is the skeleton, CSS is the clothes, and JavaScript is the brain. The site starts to think and react. Let's go!

slides.text: `const` — a variable that cannot be reassigned, like a person's name. `let` — can be changed, like age. `var` — the old way, we don't use it.

check.prompt: Which word is for a value that changes (age)?
check.explain: let can be changed, const cannot.

check.prompt: const can be reassigned, it is just a fancy word.
check.explain: const forbids reassignment — you get an error.

slides.text:
Types:
`string` — text `"Anya"`
`number` — a number `25`
`boolean` — `true` / `false`
`undefined` — a value not set yet
`null` — a value that is empty on purpose
`typeof` shows the type. Console: F12 → Console.
slides.code:
console.log(typeof "Anya"); // string
console.log(typeof 25);     // number
console.log(typeof true);   // boolean

check.prompt: Match the type and an example

slides.text: The `%` operator gives the remainder of division. To check if a number is even: `number % 2 === 0`.
`==` compares the value and ignores the type. `===` compares both the value and the type.
In projects we use only `===`: `==` often leads to bugs.
A template string uses backticks, variables go in `${}`:

check.explain: === also compares the type: a string and a number differ.

questions.prompt: Which word declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?

options: An error: const can't be reassigned

questions.prompt: var is the modern way and you should use it.
questions.explain: var is the old way, we don't use it.

questions.prompt: Match the type and what it is
What does let x; with no value mean?

questions.explain: The remainder of 10 divided by 3 is 1.

questions.prompt: How do you check a number is even?
questions.explain: An even number has remainder 0 when divided by 2.
== ignores the type, the values are equal.

questions.prompt: In projects it is better to use === instead of ==.
questions.explain: === is stricter and causes fewer bugs.

questions.prompt: Build the name output with a template string
questions.explain: A template string uses backticks with ${}.
